title: ChFC® Designation (Chartered Financial Consultant)
body: The American College of Financial Services
source: The American College of Financial Services Curriculum Catalog
summary: The premier modular financial consulting credential with comprehensive depth in small business planning, executive compensation, estate planning, and taxation across 9 modular courses (7 Core + 2 Electives).

standard.name: Standard Modular Consulting Track
standard.blurb: Complete 9 comprehensive modular courses (7 core + 2 electives), pass all 9 two-hour proctored exams, and verify 3 years of financial advisory experience.

stages.title: Stage 1: Foundational Financial Consulting Core
stages.subtitle: HS 300, HS 311, and HS 313: Fundamentals, Business Owners, and Insurance

nodes.name: HS 300: Financial Planning: Process and Environment
nodes.description: Financial planning process, code of ethics, financial statements, time value of money, education funding, and consumer credit.
topics: Personal Financial Planning Process & Fiduciary Code of Ethics
Personal Financial Statements: Balance Sheet, Cash Flow & Budgeting
Time Value of Money (TVM) Calculations for Capital Accumulation
Consumer Debt Management, Credit Scoring & Housing Financing Options
Higher Education Funding Strategies: 529 Plans, Coverdell ESAs & Aid Formulas

nodes.name: HS 311: Planning for Business Owners and Professionals
nodes.description: Choosing business entities, buy-sell agreements, corporate tax planning, business valuation, and executive compensation plans.
topics: Advising Business Entities: Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, LLCs, S/C Corps
Business Valuation Methodologies: Capitalization of Earnings & DCF Models
Buy-Sell Agreement Design: Cross-Purchase, Entity Redemption & Wait-and-See
Executive Compensation: Stock Options (ISOs/NQSOs), RSUs & Section 409A NQDC
Succession Planning: Family Business Transfer, Key Employee Buyouts & ESOPs

nodes.name: HS 313: Individual Life Insurance
nodes.description: Term, whole, universal, and variable life insurance policies; policy taxation, riders, surrender values, and insurance trust integration.
topics: Principles of Risk Analysis & Elements of Insurance Contracts
Term Life Insurance: Level, Renewable, Decreasing & Convertible Structures
Permanent Life Insurance Contracts: Whole Life Cash Values & Dividend Options
Universal Life, Variable Universal Life & Indexed Universal Life Policies
Taxation of Life Insurance: Premiums, Death Benefits & MEC 7-Pay Rules
Policy Riders, Ownership Design & Irrevocable Life Insurance Trusts (ILITs)

stages.title: Stage 2: Advanced Investment, Tax & Retirement Core
stages.subtitle: HS 321, HS 326, and HS 328: Investments, Retirement, and Taxation

nodes.name: HS 321: Investments
nodes.description: Equity and debt valuation, mutual funds, asset allocation, modern portfolio theory, performance measurement, and market efficiency.
topics: Financial Markets, Securities Exchanges, Mutual Funds & Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs)
Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT), Efficient Frontier & Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)
Fixed-Income Securities Analysis: Bond Pricing, Yield Curves, Duration & Convexity
Equity Valuation Models: Dividend Discount Models (DDM) & Free Cash Flow Models
Portfolio Performance Evaluation: Sharpe Ratio, Treynor Ratio & Jensen's Alpha
Federal Income Taxation of Investments: Capital Gains, Dividends & Tax-Loss Harvesting

nodes.name: HS 326: Planning for Retirement Needs
nodes.description: Qualified retirement plans (401k, defined benefit), IRAs, Social Security optimization, distribution rules, and required minimum distributions.
topics: Employer Qualified Retirement Plans: Defined Benefit vs. Defined Contribution (401k)
Small Business Retirement Options: SEP-IRAs, SIMPLE IRAs & Solo 401(k) Plans
Individual Retirement Accounts: Traditional Deductible IRAs vs. Roth IRAs
Social Security Optimization: Benefit Formulas, Full Retirement Age & Spousal Rules
Retirement Distribution Planning: RMD Rules (SECURE 2.0) & Sustainable Withdrawal Rates

nodes.name: HS 328: Investments & Taxation
nodes.description: Federal income taxation of individuals, property transactions, capital gains and losses, tax-advantaged investments, and AMT.
topics: Unified Federal Transfer Tax Architecture: Gift Tax, Estate Tax & Unified Credits
Estate Transfer Mechanisms: Wills, Probate Administration & Titling Modes
Trust Planning: Revocable Living Trusts, Irrevocable Trusts & Bypass Trusts
Irrevocable Life Insurance Trusts (ILITs) & Crummey Power Administration
Generation-Skipping Transfer Tax (GSTT) Planning & GSTT Exemption Allocations
Advanced Transfer Vehicles: GRATs, QPRTs, Family Limited Partnerships (FLPs) & CRTs

stages.title: Stage 3: Estate Planning & Specialized Electives
stages.subtitle: HS 330, HS 347, and Elective: Estate, Contemporary Applications & Elective

nodes.name: HS 330: Fundamentals of Estate Planning
nodes.description: Wills, probate, revocable and irrevocable trusts, gift and estate taxes, generation-skipping transfer tax, and charitable giving vehicles.
topics: Legal Foundations of Estate Planning: Wills, Holographic Wills & Codicils
Incapacity Planning: Durable Powers of Attorney, Healthcare Directives & Living Wills
Fiduciary Roles: Selection, Duties & Liabilities of Executors, Trustees & Guardians
Property Titling Strategies: JTWROS, Tenancy in Common & Tenancy by Entirety
Post-Mortem Estate Planning: Disclaimers, Sec 303 Stock Redemptions & Sec 6166

nodes.name: HS 347: Contemporary Applications in Financial Planning
nodes.description: Capstone case study course integrating all areas of personal financial planning into customized client solution blueprints.
topics: Comprehensive Client Case Study Synthesis across All 7 Planning Disciplines
Integrated Plan Construction: Cash Flow Modeling, Tax Shelters & Net Worth Tracking
Behavioral Financial Counseling: Identifying Heuristics & Cognitive Biases
Specialized Client Advisory: Unmarried Couples, Second Marriages & Blended Families
Elder Financial Planning, Long-Term Care Logistics & Incapacity Asset Protection

nodes.name: Modular Elective (HS 325 or HS 334)
nodes.description: Candidate selects one elective: HS 325 (Nonqualified Deferred Compensation and Executive Benefits) or HS 334 (Estate Planning Applications).
topics: Executive Compensation Planning (HS 325): Rabbi Trusts, SERPs & Golden Parachutes
Estate Planning Applications (HS 334): Dynasty Trusts & Asset Protection Trusts
Special Needs Financial Planning: First/Third-Party SNTs, ABLE Accounts & SSI Rules
Financial Aspects of Aging: Gerontological Wealth Planning & Medicaid Spend-Down

stages.title: Stage 4: Experience & Designation Award
stages.subtitle: 3 Years Qualifying Experience + American College Code of Ethics

nodes.name: 3 Years Full-Time Financial Advisory Experience
nodes.description: Demonstrate at least 3 years of full-time professional experience in financial planning, insurance, investments, banking, or accounting.
topics: 36 Months Advisory Work Verification
Supervisory Attestation

nodes.name: ChFC® Designation Conferred & Ethics Pledge
nodes.description: Award of the Chartered Financial Consultant (ChFC®) designation and commitment to The American College Code of Ethics and Professional Pledge.
topics: ChFC Designation Conferred
American College Professional Pledge
30 Hours Biennial PACE Recertification
